# Caesium Command Line Tools

**caesiumclt** is a powerful command-line tool for image compression that delivers exceptional results
with minimal effort. Whether you need pixel-perfect lossless compression or aggressive size reduction, caesiumclt has
you covered.

## ✨ Features

- **Multiple Compression Modes**
    - 🔍 Quality-based lossy compression
    - 💎 Lossless compression—preserve image quality while reducing size
    - 📏 Maximum size compression - target specific file sizes

- **Advanced Image Processing**
    - 📐 Resize images with multiple options (width, height, long/short edge)
    - 🔄 Convert between formats (JPEG, PNG, WebP)
    - 🏷️ EXIF metadata preservation

- **Workflow Optimization**
    - *️⃣ Recursive directory compression
    - 📁 Folder structure preservation
    - 🕒 File timestamp preservation
    - 📝 Custom suffix for output files
    - ⚡ Fast and customizable multithreaded processing

### Supported Formats

| Format   | Lossy | Lossless |
|----------|:-----:|:--------:|
| **JPEG** |   ✅   |    ✅     |
| **PNG**  |   ✅   |    ✅     |
| **WebP** |   ✅   |    ✅     |
| **GIF**  |   ✅   |    ❌     |

## 🚀 Getting Started

### Binaries

Download the latest binaries from the [release page](https://github.com/Lymphatus/caesium-clt/releases).

**Supported platforms:**

- Windows (x86_64)
- macOS (x86_64/aarch64)
- Linux (x86_64/aarch64)

## 📖 Usage

### Command-Line Options

#### Compression (at least one is required)

- `-q, --quality <QUALITY>`  
  Sets compression quality between 0 and 100. Higher the value, better the quality and bigger the file size.
- `--lossless`  
  Perform lossless compression. Some file formats may not support this or result in bigger file sizes.
- `--max-size <MAX_SIZE>`  
  Attempts to compress the image to the nearest size in bytes without exceeding it. If the requested size is too small,
  it will output the smallest possible result.

#### Advanced compression

- `--jpeg-chroma-subsampling <JPEG_CHROMA_SUBSAMPLING>`  
  Sets the chroma subsampling for JPEG files. Possible values are:
    - `4:4:4`
    - `4:2:2`
    - `4:2:0`
    - `4:1:1`
    - `auto`

- `--jpeg-baseline`  
  Forces the output to be in baseline JPEG format instead of progressive.

- `--png-opt-level <PNG_OPT_LEVEL>`  
  Sets the optimization level for PNG files. Higher values result in better compression but take longer to complete.
  Possible values are between 0 and 6. Default is 3.
- `--zopfli`  
  Use zopfli when optimizing PNG files. It may take a very long time to complete.

#### Metadata

- `-e, --exif`  
  Keeps EXIF metadata info during compression, if present. This can slightly increase the output file size.
- `--keep-dates`  
  Keeps the original last modified and last accessed date information, if possible.
- `--strip-icc`  
  Strips all ICC profile information on JPG, regardless of `-e` flag.

#### Resizing

- `--width <WIDTH>`  
  Sets the width of the output image. If height is not set, it will preserve the aspect ratio. Can't be used with
  `--long-edge` or `--short-edge`.
- `--height <HEIGHT>`  
  Sets the height of the output image. If width is not set, it will preserve the aspect ratio. Can't be used with
  `--long-edge` or `--short-edge`.
- `--long-edge <LONG_EDGE>`  
  Sets the size of the longest edge of the image. It is aware of rotation metadata. Can't be used with `--width` or
  `--height` or `--short-edge`.
- `--short-edge <SHORT_EDGE>`  
  Sets the size of the shortest edge of the image. It is aware of rotation metadata. Can't be used with `--width` or
  `--height` or `--long-edge`.
- `--no-upscale`  
  Prevent upscaling the image when resizing

#### Destination

- `-o, --output <OUTPUT>`  
  Sets the output folder. If the folder does not exist, it will be created. Can't be used with `--same-folder-as-input`.
- `--same-folder-as-input`  
  Sets the output folder to be the same as the input folder. WARNING: this can potentially overwrite the original files
  if a suffix is not set. Overwritten files CANNOT be recovered.
- `--suffix <SUFFIX>`  
  Adds a suffix to the output filename, before the file extension.
- `-S, --keep-structure`  
  Preserves the folder tree structure of the input files. Can be used only with `-R`.
- `-O, --overwrite <OVERWRITE>`  
  Sets the overwrite policy if the output file already exists. Possible values are:
    - `all`: Always overwrite
    - `never`: Never overwrite
    - `bigger`: Overwrite only if the file to be overwritten is bigger
- `--min-savings <MIN_SAVINGS>`

- `--min-savings <MIN_SAVINGS>`  
  Skip writing the output file if the compression savings are below the specified threshold.
  This is useful to prevent repeated re-compression from degrading image quality.  
  Supported formats:
    - Percentage (supports decimals): `10%`, `1.5%`, `0.1%`
    - Size with unit: `100KB`, `1MB`, `500KiB`
    - Plain number (interpreted as bytes): `1000`, `50000`
- `--format <FORMAT>`  
  Converts the original image to the selected format. Possible values are:
    - `jpeg`
    - `png`
    - `webp`
    - `original` (default, no changes)

#### Other

- `-R, --recursive`  
  If the input is a folder, scan its subfolders too.
- `-d, --dry-run`  
  Do not write output files, only simulate the process.
- `--threads <THREADS>`  
  Specify the number of parallel jobs. The maximum is the number of processors available. `0` means that the application
  will try to guess the maximum number of parallel jobs available. Default is `0`.
- `-Q, --quiet`  
  Suppress all output. Overrides `--verbose`.
- `--verbose <VERBOSE>`  
  Select how much output you want to see. Possible values are:
    - `0`: Suppress all output
    - `1`: Show only progress and final results
    - `2`: Show also skipped and error messages
    - `3`: Print all
- `-h, --help`  
  Print help. A summary can be seen with `-h`.
- `-V, --version`  
  Print version.

### Examples

**Lossless compression:**

```bash
# Compress a single image
$ caesiumclt --lossless -o output/ image.jpg

# Compress with metadata preservation
$ caesiumclt --lossless -e --keep-dates -o output/ image.jpg

# Compress a directory recursively
$ caesiumclt --lossless -R -o output/ Pictures

# Preserve folder structure
$ caesiumclt --lossless -RS -o output/ Pictures
```

**Lossy compression:**

```bash
# Compress with quality setting
$ caesiumclt -q 80 -o output/ image.jpg

# Compress multiple images with a specific quality
$ caesiumclt -q 75 -o output/ image1.jpg image2.png image3.webp

# Compress with suffix to avoid overwriting originals
$ caesiumclt -q 85 --suffix _compressed --same-folder-as-input image.jpg
```

**Format conversion:**

```bash
# Convert images to WebP format with quality setting
$ caesiumclt -q 85 --format webp -o output/ Pictures/*.jpg

# Convert PNG to JPEG with maximum quality
$ caesiumclt -q 100 --format jpeg -o output/ image.png
```

**Resizing options:**

```bash
# Resize to specific width (maintaining aspect ratio)
$ caesiumclt --lossless --width 1920 -o output/ image.jpg

# Resize to specific height (maintaining aspect ratio)
$ caesiumclt -q 90 --height 1080 -o output/ image.jpg

# Resize by longest edge (useful for mixed portrait/landscape photos)
$ caesiumclt -q 85 --long-edge 1500 -o output/ Pictures/*.jpg

# Resize by shortest edge
$ caesiumclt -q 85 --short-edge 800 -o output/ Pictures/*.jpg
```

**Advanced options:**


import subprocess, shutil, os
def scan_out(path, recursive=True):
    shutil.rmtree("/tmp/out2",ignore_errors=True)
    args=["./executable","-q","80","-o","/tmp/out2","--verbose","3","--threads","2"]
    if recursive: args.append("-R")
    args.append(path)
    r=subprocess.run(args, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30)
    return [l.split()[1] for l in r.stdout.splitlines() if l.startswith("[")]
def build():
    shutil.rmtree("/tmp/in3",ignore_errors=True)
    os.makedirs("/tmp/in3/mid",exist_ok=True)

        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(p),exist_ok=True)

print("ls -U mid", os.listdir("/tmp/in3/mid"))
print("scan recursive", scan_out("/tmp/in3"))
print("scan nonrec", scan_out("/tmp/in3",False))
# repeated
print("scan recursive2", scan_out("/tmp/in3"))

import subprocess, shutil, os, glob
EXE="/workspace/executable"
def run(args, cwd="/workspace"):
    r=subprocess.run([EXE]+args, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30, cwd=cwd)
    print(args, "exit",r.returncode, repr(r.stdout), repr(r.stderr))
    return r
def prep(out="/tmp/out2"):
    shutil.rmtree(out,ignore_errors=True); os.makedirs(out)
    # precreate existing output
    with open(out+"/p0.png","wb") as f: f.write(b"EXISTING-12345") # 14 bytes?
    return out

# overwrite all (default)
prep(); run(["-q","80","-o","/tmp/out2","--verbose","3","/tmp/ref/p0.png"]); print("size",os.path.getsize("/tmp/out2/p0.png"))
# never
prep(); run(["-q","80","-o","/tmp/out2","--verbose","3","-O","never","/tmp/ref/p0.png"]); print(open("/tmp/out2/p0.png","rb").read())
for lvl in ["0","1","2","3"]:
    prep(); run(["-q","80","-o","/tmp/out2","--verbose",lvl,"-O","never","/tmp/ref/p0.png"])
# bigger: existing bigger than new output (19554) ? existing file size 14 -> smaller, so ? Logic: Overwrite only if existing file is bigger (than what? compressed output? or input?) Precreate big file 100k
prep()
with open("/tmp/out2/p0.png","wb") as f: f.write(b"X"*100000)
run(["-q","80","-o","/tmp/out2","--verbose","3","-O","bigger","/tmp/ref/p0.png"]); print("after big existing size",os.path.getsize("/tmp/out2/p0.png"))
prep()
with open("/tmp/out2/p0.png","wb") as f: f.write(b"X"*10000)
run(["-q","80","-o","/tmp/out2","--verbose","3","-O","bigger","/tmp/ref/p0.png"]); print("after small existing size",os.path.getsize("/tmp/out2/p0.png"), open("/tmp/out2/p0.png","rb").read(10))
# dry run
prep()
os.remove("/tmp/out2/p0.png")
run(["-q","80","-o","/tmp/out2","--verbose","3","-d","/tmp/ref/p0.png"]); print("exists after dry", os.path.exists("/tmp/out2/p0.png"))
# dry + never with existing?
prep(); run(["-q","80","-o","/tmp/out2","--verbose","3","-d","-O","never","/tmp/ref/p0.png"])
PY"}

import struct
# PNG
with open("/tmp/ref/p0.png","rb") as f: d=f.read()
print("PNG", struct.unpack(">IIBBBBB", d[16:29]))
# JPEG scan markers
data=open("/tmp/ref/j0.JPG","rb").read()
i=2
while i < len(data):
    if data[i]!=0xFF: i+=1; continue
    m=data[i+1]
    if m in (0xD8,0xD9) or 0xD0<=m<=0xD7:
        print(hex(m)); i+=2; continue
    ln=struct.unpack(">H", data[i+2:i+4])[0]
    print(f"marker FF{m:02X} len {ln} at {i}", data[i+4:i+20][:10])
    if m in (0xC0,0xC1,0xC2):
        print(" SOF prec",data[i+4],"h,w",struct.unpack(">HH",data[i+5:i+9]),"comp",data[i+9])
    if m==0xDA: break
    i+=2+ln
# WebP
d=open("/tmp/ref/w0.webp","rb").read()
print("webp", d[:60])
# parse VP8 frame tag etc width 14 bits at ?
print("VP8 width height", struct.unpack("<H", d[26:28])[0] & 0x3fff, struct.unpack("<H", d[28:30])[0] & 0x3fff)
# GIF
d=open("/tmp/ref/g1.gif","rb").read()
print("GIF w h", struct.unpack("<HH", d[6:10]), "packed", d[10])
# count frames 0x21, 2C
print("gif trailer blocks rough image sep count", d.count(b'\x2c')) # unreliable
# TIFF
d=open("/tmp/ref/t0.tif","rb").read()
print("tiff header", d[:8])
PY"}

import struct
# crude GIF block parser
def parse(p):
    d=open(p,"rb").read()
    pos=13
    # packed 10: GCT size
    packed=d[10]; gct_size=3*2**((packed & 0x07)+1) if packed & 0x80 else 0
    print(p, "len",len(d),"wh",struct.unpack("<HH",d[6:10]),"packed",packed,"gct",gct_size, "bg",d[11],"aspect",d[12])
    pos+=gct_size
    frames=0; exts={}
    while pos<len(d):
        b=d[pos]
        if b==0x3B: print(" trailer",pos); break
        elif b==0x21: # ext
            label=d[pos+1]; size=d[pos+2]; exts[label]=exts.get(label,0)+1; pos+=3+size
            while True:
                sz=d[pos]; pos+=1
                if sz==0: break
                pos+=sz
        elif b==0x2C:
            x,y,w,h,pk=struct.unpack("<HHHHB", d[pos+1:pos+10]); frames+=1
            local=3*2**((pk&0x07)+1) if pk&0x80 else 0
            pos+=10+local
            lzw_min=d[pos]; pos+=1
            total=0
            while True:
                sz=d[pos]; pos+=1
                if sz==0: break
                total+=sz; pos+=sz
            if frames<=3: print(" frame",x,y,w,h,pk,"lzwmin",lzw_min,"data",total)
        else:
            print(" unknown",hex(b),"at",pos); break
    print(" frames",frames,"exts",exts)

import struct, subprocess, shutil, os
def parse(p):
    d=open(p,"rb").read(); pos=13; packed=d[10]; gct=3*2**((packed&7)+1) if packed&0x80 else 0; pos+=gct; frames=0; delays=[]; disposals=[]; trans=[]
    while pos<len(d):
        b=d[pos]
        if b==0x3B: break
        elif b==0x21:
            label=d[pos+1]
            if label==0xF9:
                sz=d[pos+2]; block=d[pos+3:pos+3+sz]; delays.append(struct.unpack("<H",block[1:3])[0]); disposals.append((block[0]>>2)&7); trans.append(block[3] if block[0]&1 else None)
            pos+=3+d[pos+2]
            while d[pos]!=0: pos+=1+d[pos]; 
            pos+=1
        elif b==0x2C:
            w,h,pk=struct.unpack("<HHB", d[pos+5:pos+10])[0], struct.unpack("<HH", d[pos+5:pos+9]), d[pos+9]
            # simplify
            x,y,fw,fh,pk2=struct.unpack("<HHHHB", d[pos+1:pos+10]); frames+=1; local=3*2**((pk2&7)+1) if pk2&0x80 else 0; pos+=10+local; pos+=1

    print(p, len(d), "frames",frames, "delays",delays[:5], "disposals",disposals[:5], "trans idx",trans[:5])

A fast and efficient lossy and/or lossless image compression tool

Usage: executable [OPTIONS] <--quality <QUALITY>|--lossless|--max-size <MAX_SIZE>> <--output <OUTPUT>|--same-folder-as-input> [FILES]...

Arguments:
  [FILES]...  Input files or directories to process

Options:
  -q, --quality <QUALITY>
          Compression quality [0-100], higher values mean better quality
      --lossless
          Use lossless compression (may increase file size for some formats)
      --max-size <MAX_SIZE>
          Target maximum file size in bytes or human-readable format (e.g., 100KB, 0.5MB)
      --width <WIDTH>
          Output image width in pixels (preserves the aspect ratio if height not set)
      --height <HEIGHT>
          Output image height in pixels (preserves the aspect ratio if width not set)
      --long-edge <LONG_EDGE>
          Size in pixels for the longest edge of the image
      --short-edge <SHORT_EDGE>
          Size in pixels for the shortest edge of the image
      --no-upscale
          Prevents upscaling of the image when resizing
  -o, --output <OUTPUT>
          Output directory path
      --same-folder-as-input
          Use input file's directory as output (WARNING: may overwrite originals)
      --format <FORMAT>
          Convert to the selected output format or keep the original [default: original] [possible values: jpeg, png, gif, webp, tiff, original]
      --png-opt-level <PNG_OPT_LEVEL>
          PNG optimization level [0-6], higher values provide better compression [default: 3]
      --jpeg-chroma-subsampling <JPEG_CHROMA_SUBSAMPLING>
          Chroma subsampling for JPEG files [default: auto] [possible values: 4:4:4, 4:2:2, 4:2:0, 4:1:1, auto]
      --jpeg-baseline
          Output baseline JPEG instead of progressive (default)
      --zopfli
          Use zopfli for PNG optimization (significantly slower but better compression)
  -e, --exif
          Keep EXIF metadata during compression
      --keep-dates
          Preserve original file timestamps
      --strip-icc
          Strips ICC profile info on JPG files, ignoring the -e flag
      --suffix <SUFFIX>
          Add suffix to output filenames
  -R, --recursive
          Scan subfolders recursively when input is a directory
  -S, --keep-structure
          Preserve directory structure (requires -R/--recursive)
  -d, --dry-run
          Simulate compression without writing files
      --threads <THREADS>
          Number of parallel jobs (0 = auto-detect, max = available processors) [default: 0]
  -O, --overwrite <OVERWRITE>
          Policy for handling existing output files [default: all] [possible values: all, never, bigger]
      --min-savings <MIN_SAVINGS>
          Minimum compression savings required to write an output file. Use percentage (e.g., '10%', '1.5%'), absolute size (e.g., '100KB', '1MB'), or plain number as bytes
  -Q, --quiet
          Suppress all output
      --verbose <VERBOSE>
          Verbosity level: 0 = quiet, 1 = progress only, 2 = errors only, 3 = all [default: 1]
  -h, --help
          Print help (see more with '--help')
  -V, --version
          Print version

def gifinfo(p):
    d=open(p,"rb").read(); packed=d[10]; gct=2**((packed&7)+1) if packed&0x80 else 0
    # count frames and local pal sizes
    pos=13+(3*gct if gct else 0); frames=[]
    while pos<len(d):
        b=d[pos]
        if b==0x3B: break

            while d[pos]!=0: pos+=1+d[pos]

            while d[pos]!=0: pos+=1+d[pos]
            pos+=1

import subprocess, shutil, os
ORIG="/tmp/origtest/executable"; NEW="/tmp/newtest/executable"

def setup_env(root):
    shutil.rmtree(root,ignore_errors=True); os.makedirs(root+"/in/sub",exist_ok=True)
    # copies
    shutil.copy("/tmp/ref/p0.png",root+"/in/a.png"); shutil.copy("/tmp/ref/j0.JPG",root+"/in/b.jpg"); shutil.copy("/tmp/ref/w0.webp",root+"/in/sub/c.webp")
    open(root+"/in/fake.png","wb").write(b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n'+b'\x00'*20)
    open(root+"/in/text.txt","w").write("hello world, not image")
    shutil.copy("/tmp/ref/p0.png",root+"/in/sub/d.png")

def run_pair(label,args,cwd=None,prep=None):
    results=[]
    for exe,root in [(ORIG,"/tmp/env_o"),(NEW,"/tmp/env_n")]:
        shutil.rmtree(root,ignore_errors=True); os.makedirs(root)
        setup_env(root)
        if prep: prep(root)
        a=[x.replace("{ROOT}",root) for x in args]
        r=subprocess.run([exe]+a,capture_output=True,text=True,cwd=cwd.replace("{ROOT}",root) if cwd else None)
        # normalize root path differences in stdout/stderr
        out=r.stdout.replace(root,"{ROOT}"); err=r.stderr.replace(root,"{ROOT}")
        # Also cwd /workspace differences? none
        files=[]
        outdir=root+"/out"
        if os.path.exists(outdir):
            for rr,_,fs in os.walk(outdir):
                for f in fs: files.append(os.path.relpath(os.path.join(rr,f),outdir))
        results.append((r.returncode,out,err,sorted(files)))
    if results[0]!=results[1]:
        print("DIFF",label)
        print(" orig",results[0]); print(" new ",results[1])
    else:
        print("OK",label)

run_pair("dir scan verbose1",["-q","80","-o","{ROOT}/out","{ROOT}/in"])

fn convert_decode_error(data: &[u8], detected: Format, orig: CompError) -> CompError {
    let full = match detected {
        Format::Png => {
            // check strict signature
            if data.len() < 8 || &data[0..8] != b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n" {
                "The image format could not be determined".to_string()
            } else if data.len() < 33 && data.len() >= 16 && &data[12..16] == b"IHDR" {
                "unexpected end of file".to_string()
            } else if data.len() >= 16 && &data[12..16] != b"IHDR" {
                let t = &data[12..16];
                let fmt_byte = |b: u8| -> String {
                    if b == 0 { "\\0".to_string() } else if (32..127).contains(&b) { (b as char).to_string() } else { format!("\\u{{{}}}", b) }
                };
                let type_str: String = t.iter().map(|&b| fmt_byte(b)).collect();
                format!("Format error decoding Png: ChunkType {{ type: {}, critical: {}, private: {}, reserved: false, safecopy: false }} chunk appeared before IHDR chunk", type_str, (t[0] & 32) == 0, (t[1] & 32) != 0)
            } else {
                format!("Format error decoding Png: {}", orig.message)
            }
        }
        Format::Jpeg => {
            // Segment truncation as reported by the JPEG decoder used for conversions
            let mut trunc: Option<(usize, usize)> = None; // (expected, found)
            let mut invalid_len: Option<u16> = None;
            if data.len() >= 4 && data[0] == 0xFF && data[1] == 0xD8 {
                let mut pos = 2usize;
                while pos + 4 <= data.len() {
                    if data[pos] != 0xFF { break; }
                    let m = data[pos + 1];
                    if m == 0xDA { break; }
                    if m == 0xD8 || (0xD0..=0xD7).contains(&m) { pos += 2; continue; }
                    let len = u16::from_be_bytes([data[pos + 2], data[pos + 3]]);
                    if len < 2 { invalid_len = Some(len); break; }
                    if pos + 2 + len as usize > data.len() {
                        let expected = (len as usize).saturating_sub(8);
                        let found = data.len().saturating_sub(pos + 10);
